headline: South Asia: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
- Australia: At least eight killed as Russia and Ukraine trade strikes.
- Asia: France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
- Military Times, one day ago: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
Unauthorized users accessed files containing the personal information of U.S. military personnel, a new breach notification letter warns.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Army awards Palantir $48.1M to modernize ammo management.
The tech company has built AI software designed to process data for targeting and decision-making, and now, managing ammo.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Army identifies 19th US service member to die amid Iran war.
The U.S. Army identified the 19th U.S. service member to die while deployed in support of the war with Iran.
- Military Times, one day ago: 8 sailors attempted suicide aboard ships from Lincoln strike group, Cao says.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed that eight sailors from the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Putin claims Ukraine attacked polling stations in Russia.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Putin claims Ukraine attacked polling stations in Russia.
Putin claimed Ukrainian strikes on 19-20 September damaged a school used as a polling station and homes of election officials.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian drone strikes school in Kyiv Oblast, causing major fire – photo.
A Russian drone hit Ivanivka school No. 2 in Kyiv Oblast's Vyshhorod district, sparking a large fire; no children were harmed.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Number injured in Russian attacks on Kyiv rises to 57, with 7 killed.
SEO Description: Russian drone attacks on Kyiv on 25 September killed seven people and injured 57, including two children.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Two Russian guided bombs hit different districts of Sumy: 8 injured, including 3 children.
Two strikes hit separate parts of Sumy, damaging houses and an educational facility; rescue teams continue working at both sites.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons.
The president said he received a positive and constructive response from the EU during his diplomatic talks this week.
- Balkan Insight, 7 hours ago: Week in Review: Spyware, AI and Arrests.
Tech concerns mount over elections in Serbia, spy chief’s arrest tests Albania’s NATO ties, protests over court verdicts continue in Kosovo and North Macedonia mulls impact of dangerous virus, our selection of Balkan Insight’s Premium stories this week shows.

Berlin strebt einen breit aufgestellten Verbund von Handelspartnern an, während Madrid ein gestaffeltes System vorschlägt, bei dem in der EU hergestellte Waren Vorrang genießen.

- Africanews, 15 hours ago: Ethiopian president warns of 'interference' amid renewed Tigray fighting.
Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Taye Atske Selassie blamed 'external actors' for renewed conflict in the region.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
Ethiopian forces battled overnight to repel an assault by Tigray rebels in the Afar region, a humanitarian source said on Friday, with reports of an internet blackout in the north of the country. Rebels in the northern Tigray region seized local airports and launched attacks into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara this week, saying they were once again in a “full-blown war” with the federal government. Locals fear a repeat of the telecoms blackout and supplies blockade imposed on Tigray during the last civil war in 2020-2022 that killed an estimated 600,000 people.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Info ministry dismisses Afghan claims of destroying Pakistani post near border in Balochistan as 'fake'.
The information ministry dismissed on Friday claims by the Afghan defence ministry of a Pakistani post having been destroyed near the Spin Boldak border — the frontier between Balochistan and Kandahar — as “fake and fabricated”. The information ministry also took note of Afghan claims that there had been no casualties among the Afghan forces in the latest episode of clash between the two sides. “The claim is fake and fabricated.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 13 hours ago: Security forces kill several Afghan Taliban fighters in retaliatory action along Balochistan border: sources.
Pakistani troops responded to an act of aggression along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Balochistan and killed several Afghan Taliban on Thursday, state media reported, citing sources. State-run APP reported, citing sources, that the Afghan Taliban attempted to enter the Pakistani territory in Balochistan’s Gulistan sector and carry out an act of aggression. Meanwhile, officials also reported attacks on some border posts in Pakistan. The APP report said in retaliatory action, several Afghan Taliban fighters were killed.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Any attempt to divert Pakistan’s water to be treated as act of war, India ‘must make no mistake about it’: PM at UNGA.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that any attempt by India to divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”. “Any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the waters will be treated as an act of war. India must make no mistake about it,” he said during a speech at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, where he called attention to the neighbouring country’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance.

Frustrated by low-quality materials, careless craftsmanship, and escalating prices, some young women in China are taking matters into their own hands by learning to sew their own underwear, accessories, and handbags. This summer, a surge of sewing enthusiasts flocked to RedNote to showcase their handmade creations. - Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Who is Tommy “Gun” McMillen? Meet UFC’s 12-0 featherweight prospect.
Tommy 'Gun' McMillen is building his reputation in the UFC featherweight division with an undefeated record. He began his combat sports journey at a young age, excelling in wrestling and boxing. McMillen has won all three of his UFC fights, showcasing his striking and finishing abilities. He broke a UFC record for significant strikes landed in a three-round fight during his bout with Alberto Montes.

Donald Trump told Xi Jinping that any assistance China provides to Iran is unacceptable during his visit. The two leaders held a closed-door meeting to discuss various critical global issues, including trade and military matters. Trump organized a state dinner attended by key US technology executives to enhance relations. The visit coincided with China's Mid-Autumn Festival, marking a time for family gatherings and festivities.

He’s ready for blowback On the eve of publication of his new book, Bruce Pascoe is steeling himself for potential controversy that could rival the bitter storm that battered and bruised him for years over the 2014 book that rewrote Australian history: Dark Emu.
